about: Okay Grandpa, Let's Get You to Bed uses a stock photo of an elderly man in a flat cap and light blue shirt shuffling along a garden path with a walker while a younger man gently holds his arm. The caption treats an outdated opinion, trend or piece of tech as the old man, and the reply as the patient helper steering him off to sleep. It is a polite roast: you are not arguing with the take, just escorting it out because its time has clearly passed.
origin: It grew out of an older grandma version of the joke, built on a stock photo of an elderly woman with a walker. This one swaps in a grandfather and keeps the condescending bedtime line.
usage:
The top box holds the outdated statement, usually in quotes or as something the grandpa character says: an old meme, a dead platform, a retro opinion. The bottom box is the response, nearly always "okay grandpa, let's get you to bed" or a close variation.

It works best when the top line is something people genuinely used to believe or love, so the gentle dismissal feels earned. Tech history, gaming nostalgia and sports takes from decades ago are all good material.
